cost_table.description: N5 design-target machine for the HBM role of the analytical anchor pair Qwen3-8B/ROM-N5-native-SRAMKV-array-pipeline-x5-romfill vs Qwen3-8B/b200_sxm-x3-tensor (Qwen3-8B, batch 1, context 8192).  DERIVED, NOT MEASURED: every parameter here is an analytical value divided by a stated denominator or an explicit statement that the analytical model prices no counterpart, and every entry carries its derivation in `note` and its technology.json grade in `analytical_grade`.  Nothing in this file is characterized; the measured SKY130 and ASAP7 tables are untouched and describe a different machine.  Generated by tools/derive_cycle_machine.py from results/roofline/n5_vs_b200/analytical.json; run that tool with --check to verify this file still matches the anchor it claims.

address_placement.note: descriptor base_address values were distinct and were used

implementation_identity.note: TA-ABI3-OPCONV-1 amendment A7: the blocked contract's association is fixed by an implementation identity -- library, version, device and shape -- and does not claim portability across implementations. Two runs of this identity are bit-identical; a run on another identity is not guaranteed to be

numerics.rule: TA-ABI3-OPCONV-1 amendment A7: anything claiming bit-exactness must name which of the two declared contracts it means, and an execution report records the implementation identity that fixes the blocked contract's association

plausibility.rule: total_cycles / (bytes_moved / peak_bytes_per_cycle); a total far above this floor is dominated by the conflict and stall model, not by the program's work

acyclic_waits.rule: in-order issue plus single-assignment events: a wait is acyclic iff every producer is signalled strictly earlier in program order

bounded_queue_occupancy.rule: issue is credit-gated: an engine descriptor enters a queue only when occupancy is below min(queue_depth, max_outstanding), so occupancy is bounded by construction

no_zero_latency_global_operations.rule: single-chip topology has no inter-node fabric; no global barrier or collective is expressible, so none is modelled as zero-latency

clock.frequency_hz.name: clock.frequency_hz
clock.frequency_hz.note: 3 sequencer cycles (sequencer.fetch_cycles + decode_cycles + issue_cycles, the cycle model's per-instruction front end) divided by technology.json#latency.sequencer_issue_decode_s = 3e-09 s.  The analytical model states no clock; this is the one analytical quantity that fixes one.  Every rate below is an analytical B/s or ops/s divided by this clock, so a different clock would move the per-cycle numbers and leave every derived TIME unchanged.

engine.attention.bytes_per_cycle.name: engine.attention.bytes_per_cycle
engine.attention.bytes_per_cycle.note: The analytical model prices no engine byte-port bandwidth.  Both machines are given the larger of the pair's weight-path rates (9.542400e+13 B/s) so that no simulated time is attributed to an engine port the analytical model does not model.  At the shipped 64 B/cycle this would throttle DMA to 6.400e+10 B/s, 1491x below the ROM array it drains.

engine.attention.fixed_latency_cycles.name: engine.attention.fixed_latency_cycles
engine.attention.fixed_latency_cycles.note: technology.json#latency.pipeline_fill_drain_s 3.2e-08 s + one global wire traversal sqrt(reticle.area_mm2) x global_wire_delay_s_per_mm = 4.282231e-09 s, the analytical array-pass boundary 3.628223e-08 s, times the clock = 36.2822 cycles.  The analytical model charges 4 of these per layer; the cycle model charges one per engine instruction and has no per-layer hook, so the difference between the deployment's instructions per layer and 4 is a reported residual, not a tuned parameter.

engine.tensor.work_per_lane_cycle.name: engine.tensor.work_per_lane_cycle
engine.tensor.work_per_lane_cycle.note: compute roof / (lanes x clock), in work-counter units.  The roof is the design point's OWN arithmetic over the design point's OWN published time: bf16 15136811008 = 15136811008 operations / component_times_s.compute 0.00015861700976394524 s = 9.5429935481e+13 ops/s.  That identity is exact by construction, which is the point: a literal 'bf16' index into operations_by_canonical_format raises on a w4a8 design point and a literal 'bf16' compute density prices one 2.7x too slow WITHOUT raising.  Cross-checked against the technology derivation the study built the term from -- sum over formats of ops_f / (area_fractions.compute 0.3131246661498641 x silicon_area_mm2 4075.0 x compute_ops_s_per_mm2[f] x efficiencies.compute 0.55), times token_slots 5 -- which gives 1.586170097639452e-04 s against the published 1.586170097639452e-04 s, agreeing to +0.000e+00 relative.  Units: the cost table declares this parameter in work/lane/cycle and the shipped characterized value was measured as (tensor.multiplications + tensor.additions) / cycles; the analytical operations count is a work count too, at 2 operations per active parameter (the multiply-and-add fallback), so no conversion is needed and none is applied.  That makes the machine's MAC rate lanes x work_per_lane_cycle / 2 x clock = 4.7714967741e+13 MAC/s.  In the cycle model this value divides the K extent (ceil(tile_depth x work_scale / work_per_lane_cycle)), so it is the reduction-tree width of one output lane -- 46.60 MACs deep -- and not a second lane count.

hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel.name: hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel
hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel.note: One HBM3E channel, taken from the GPU point and shared: points[GPU].kv_transfer_bytes_per_step / component_times_s.kv_read x token_slots 1 = 2.160000e+13 B/s of physical pool over 3 packages x 8 stacks x 8 channels = 1.125000e+11 B/s per channel = 112.5 B/cycle at this clock.  The COUNT each collapsed logical device carries is that design's provisioning divided by the slots a token traverses: the GPU role gets 192 channels for 2.160000e+13 B/s and the ROM role a single INERT channel, because its kv_store is 'sram' and its area_fractions.hbm_phy is 0.0 -- it buys no HBM at all.  The two design points buy different numbers of the SAME channel, which is why hbm.channels is the only HBM parameter the two machines are permitted to differ on.

hbm.interleave_bytes.name: hbm.interleave_bytes
hbm.interleave_bytes.note: Set equal to the HBM burst so consecutive bursts stripe across channels.

hbm.read_latency_cycles.name: hbm.read_latency_cycles
hbm.read_latency_cycles.note: The analytical layer_fixed_latency charges one KV round trip per layer: sram_access_s 2e-09 + one global traversal 4.282231e-09 = 6.282231e-09 s = 6.2822 cycles.  points[GPU] holds KV in 'hbm' and points[ROM] in 'sram'; the primitive is a round trip to whichever store holds it, so it is charged identically on both machines and is shared.

hbm.transaction_bytes.name: hbm.transaction_bytes
hbm.transaction_bytes.note: 225 B = 2 x hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel, the smallest integer burst for which the cycle model's ceil(transaction_bytes / bytes_per_cycle) is exact and no channel bandwidth is lost to quantisation.  The analytical model has no burst-size concept.

rom.arrays.name: rom.arrays
rom.arrays.note: the capability does not advertise memory.rom.arrays; taken from cost table parameter 'rom.arrays.default'.  The GPU design point 'Qwen3-8B/b200_sxm-x3-tensor' has no ROM (area_fractions.rom = 0.0).  These four rom.* values exist because the cost-table schema requires the full parameter set; no MEMORY_OBJECT in the HBM deployment is stamped StorageClass.ROM, so the ROM unit pool is never scheduled.

rom.read_latency_cycles.name: rom.read_latency_cycles
rom.read_latency_cycles.note: The analytical model prices no ROM access latency.  The ROM array is on die, so the one analytical latency primitive that applies is a global wire traversal of the reticle: sqrt(reticle.area_mm2 815.0) x global_wire_delay_s_per_mm 1.5e-10 = 4.282231e-09 s = 4.2822 cycles.

sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port.name: sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port
sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port.note: The GPU design point prices NO SRAM term and allocates no SRAM area (area_fractions.sram 0.0), so there is nothing to reproduce.  banks x ports x this rate x clock = 1.310720e+14 B/s, which exceeds every rate this pair derives (9.542994e+13 B/s) so that the activation store cannot bind and no simulated time is attributed to a store the analytical model does not price.  This is a deliberate neutralisation for a validation experiment: the derived machine is NOT a complete machine and its absolute tokens/s is an upper bound.

sram.interleave_bytes.name: sram.interleave_bytes
sram.interleave_bytes.note: Set equal to the SRAM burst so consecutive bursts stripe across ports.  See sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port.

sram.transaction_bytes.name: sram.transaction_bytes
sram.transaction_bytes.note: Set equal to sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port so the model's ceil() is exact.  See that parameter.

state.backing_storage_class.name: state.backing_storage_class
state.backing_storage_class.note: STATE objects are timed as if they lived in SRAM, unchanged from the shipped tables.  ADR-003 does not bind the placement of a state resource and the analytical model has no state term.

schedule_audit.rule: the program carries no tile loops, so every OPERATOR-driven engine instruction must name a SCHEDULE descriptor with a non-zero tile shape; a zeroed or absent mapping is a hard error

assumptions.operand_refetch: a contraction re-reads its left operand per column tile and its right operand per row tile; accumulated output is written once
assumptions.partial_tile_cost: tensor SCHEDULE dimensions are maximum blocking extents; resolved row, column and depth tails are masked
assumptions.physical_lane_activity: counted from deterministic tensor output-coordinate waves

memory_traffic.scope: tiled engine families on the reported node

physical_lane_utilisation.reason: tensor output coordinates are mapped into deterministic row-folded waves using resolved view extents; absent coordinates are masked and perform no MAC

tiling.rule: the program loops over layers, token blocks, experts and vocabulary partitions only; one engine instruction names a whole contraction and the SCHEDULE descriptor carries the tile shape, so this model is the only place tiling becomes time

unmodelled_schedule_fields.priority: recorded but not timed: the microsequencer is in-order, so a queue priority cannot reorder anything it issues
unmodelled_schedule_fields.resource_bound: recorded but not timed: ABI 3.0 does not say what unit resource_bound counts
